1: Storing programs and data in one memory means both travel on the same buses. The CPU fetches each instruction from memory, which is why the fetch-decode-execute cycle is central.
2: The program counter holds the address of the next instruction, so the CPU always knows where to fetch from. Decoding then identifies the operation, and execution carries it out.
3: RAM is volatile because its contents depend on power. It is fast working memory, which is why it holds only the programs and data in use.
4: Input devices turn real-world signals into digital data, and output devices turn digital data back into something a person can perceive. Sensors are input devices that measure physical quantities.
5: Secondary storage keeps data without power but is slower than RAM. The CPU accesses RAM directly, which is why RAM counts as primary storage.
